ai.description: Lycodon jara grows to 50 cm. It is brown with white crossbars and two rows of dark spots. Key features include a flattened head, large eyes, and a distinct white collar behind the head.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Lycodon jara* is best distinguished by its uniform, dark brown to blackish body lacking the prominent white or yellow cross-bands found on most other Indian wolf snakes.
ai.habitat: The Twin-spotted Wolf Snake inhabits moist deciduous forests, scrublands, and agricultural areas, typically ranging from lowlands up to 1,500 meters in elevation.
ai.behavior: The Twin-spotted Wolf Snake is primarily nocturnal, actively hunting small lizards and frogs under the cover of darkness.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Lycodon jara* is oviparous, typically laying clutches of 3–5 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, with hatchlings appearing shortly thereafter.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Lycodon jara* is found across northern and northeastern India, extending into the Himalayan foothills and West Bengal, typically at low to moderate elevations.
